To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the major conformer of Tachy in EPA is s-trans,s-ciscis-Tachy, not s-cis,s-trans-cis-Tachy as previously reported, and that Pre and Pro photoisomerize in EPA by the OBT, not the hula-twist (HT), mechanism.

the photoisomerization of previtamin D (Pre) in EPA at low temperatures proceeds by a one-bond twist (OBT), not hula twist (HT), mechanism, and that the major photoproduct of Pre is tZc-Tachy, not the expected cZt-Tachy.
the photoisomerizations Pre → Tachy and Pro → Tachy proceed by the OBT mechanism in contrast to the hula-twist mechanism in organic solvents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photobiology and photopharmacology of vitamin D and its derivatives.
the mechanism of photoisomerization of vitamin D3 in glassy EPA at 77 K, which is the first step of vitamin D3 photobiological activity.
the photochemistry of vitamin D3 and its precursors, and with the photoisomerizations in EPA at 4 K.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photoisomerizations are not hula-twists, but OBTs.
the photoisomerizations in EPA proceed by OBT, not by the hula-twist mechanism.
the photoisomerization of previtamin D proceeds by the OBT mechanism, not the hula-twist mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in EPA the photoisomerizations proceed by the OBT mechanism, not hula-twist.
the photochemical reactions of Pre and Pro in EPA are governed by the OBT mechanism, not by the hula-twist (HT) mechanism as previously proposed.
in EPA, photoisomerization of Pro and Pre occurs via OBT and not via hula-twist (HT) mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemical behavior of Pre in EPA differs from that in solution, and that the photochemical pathway in the glassy medium is different from the OBT mechanism in solution.
OBT, not hula-twist, is the mechanism of the photoisomerization of vitamin D3 and its precursors.
